info.name: Clinical Co-Pilot
info.description:
Conversational clinical co-pilot for OpenEMR — grounded, cited point-of-care synthesis over the OAuth2/SMART-FHIR API.

One request per public endpoint of the FastAPI service (`copilot.main:app`). Import this collection together with `clinical-copilot.postman_environment.json` and run the folders top-to-bottom for a local happy path.

### Headers
- `X-Provider-Id` — the acting provider (defaults to `admin` server-side when absent). Sourced from the `{{provider_id}}` variable.
- `X-Break-Glass-Reason` — an explicit break-glass justification. Locally, Synthea patients have no schedule, so this header is the only way the *granted* summary/conversation happy path is reachable. A blank/absent value means the normal gated path (which will refuse an out-of-panel patient).

### Streaming
The summary, conversation, and follow-up endpoints stream newline-delimited JSON (`application/x-ndjson`). Postman shows the raw stream in the response body once the stream completes.

### Chaining
Starting a conversation emits a `conversation` event whose `conversation_id` is captured by a test script into the `{{conversation_id}}` collection variable, so the "Send follow-up message" request chains automatically.

item.name: health
item.description: Liveness / readiness probes. No auth, no headers required.

request.description: Liveness probe. Returns the service `HealthStatus` (status + version). Always cheap; never touches OpenEMR.
Readiness probe. Verifies upstream dependencies (e.g. the OpenEMR OAuth/FHIR surface) are reachable before the service accepts clinical traffic.

item.name: summary
item.description: The streamed, cited patient-summary endpoint (M1 acceptance surface).

header.description: Acting provider identity (dev default `admin` if omitted).

header.value: Local smoke test — Synthea patient has no schedule
header.description: Break-glass justification. Required locally for the granted happy path; blank/absent means the normal gated path (refuses an out-of-panel patient).

request.description:
Runs the gate-first lifecycle and streams the finalized summary as newline-delimited JSON (`application/x-ndjson`):

- `headline`
- one `must_know` / `what_changed` line per claim, each carrying its `sources` (`source_id` pointers, FR-8)
- deterministic `flag` safety events (with sources)
- `caveat` hedges
- one `notice` per un-retrieved tier (FR-12 — "couldn't retrieve X")
- a closing `data_as_of` line

An out-of-panel patient streams a single `refusal` event and nothing else — no chart data leaves the gate.

request.description:
Starts a conversation. Runs the full role → panel → cache-through retrieve → summary lifecycle, pins the patient, and streams the cited summary followed by a `conversation` event carrying the `conversation_id` used for follow-ups.

The test script parses the NDJSON stream and stores `conversation_id` in the `{{conversation_id}}` collection variable so the next request chains.

An out-of-panel or role-denied request streams a single `refusal` event and pins nothing (no `conversation_id` captured).

header.description: Acting provider identity (dev default `admin` if omitted).

request.description:
Answers a follow-up over the started conversation. The pinned patient is resolved from the conversation (pronouns like "she" never re-select a chart); the answer is grounded against the retained records and each cited claim is streamed as NDJSON:

- `conversation` (echoes the id + patient)
- one `answer` line per grounded claim, each with its `sources`
- `dropped` notices for claims the grounding gate rejected
- `caveat` hedges

Body is a JSON object with a single `question` field. An unknown or expired `conversation_id` returns `404` (a JSON `{ "detail": ... }` body), not a fresh unpinned chat.

item.name: prewarm
item.description: Warm today's scheduled charts into the shared cache.

header.description: Acting provider whose schedule is warmed (dev default `admin` if omitted).

request.description:
Fetches the acting provider's schedule for today and warms each patient's `CriticalSet` into the process-wide shared cache (M2-4, FR-13), so opening one of those charts later reads a warm cache instead of waiting on the tiered FHIR retrieval.

Returns a `PrewarmReport` — counts and timings only, no clinical values. Data-only (no LLM call) and never fatal (a single chart's retrieval failing is recorded in the report, not raised).
